monthly_review.summary: This month shows increased volume and improved aerobic efficiency, but with a notable drop in training intensity and pace — indicating a strategic shift toward recovery and base-building.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 3+ time dropped sharply from 45% last month (z3+z4+z5 = 26+15+4) to just 21% this month (z3+z4+z5 = 19+2+0), signaling a deliberate reduction in threshold and VO2 max stimulus.

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s distance by 5.8 km and matched the number of runs — no additional running is needed to surpass April’s totals.

insights.title: Efficiency dipped despite higher cadence
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.66 to 13.35 m/sec/spm even as cadence rose from 142 to 146 spm — suggesting stride length decreased (e.g., recent 5.6 km run: 67.6 cm stride at 9:42/km vs 94.4 cm at 7:27/km in April), likely due to fatigue or pacing strategy.

insights.title: Strong Z1/Z2 dominance with minimal high-intensity work
insights.body: This month’s Z1+Z2 time (79%) far exceeds last month’s (55%), while Z4+Z5 dropped from 19% to 2% — confirming a clear emphasis on low-HR endurance, which supports recovery but may delay pace-specific adaptations if sustained too long.

insights.title: Cadence increased but ground contact time remains elevated
insights.body: Cadence improved (+4 spm), yet average ground contact time stayed high (~308–316 ms across recent runs), above the typical recreational benchmark of <290 ms for efficient sub-10:00/km running — indicating form economy hasn’t kept pace with turnover gains.

insights.title: Lower aerobic TE aligns with reduced HR and pace intensity
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE dropped from 3.1 to 2.7, matching the 6 bpm HR decrease and +24 sec/km pace slowdown — confirming lower physiological stress, consistent with the goal of building aerobic resilience without accumulating fatigue.

recommendations.action: Do one 5 km run at Zone 2 HR (130–138 bpm) with cadence ≥150 spm and focus on minimizing ground contact time — aim for ≤300 ms (use Garmin's real-time GCT metric if available).
recommendations.reason: Your recent runs show cadence can hit 150–154 spm (e.g., May 13 & 28), but GCT remains >308 ms — targeted practice at sustainable HR will reinforce neuromuscular efficiency.

recommendations.action: Insert one short Zone 3 interval session before month-end: 3 × 3 min @ 148–154 bpm with 90 sec walk/jog recovery.
recommendations.reason: Z3 time fell to 19% this month vs 26% last month, and your best recent pace (447 sec/km = ~7:27/km) suggests capacity for brief threshold work — this will maintain neuromuscular readiness without overstressing recovery.

recommendations.action: After your next easy run, perform 4 × 30-sec barefoot or minimalist strides on grass, focusing on quick lift-off and quiet footstrike.
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation is stable (~7.5–8.1 cm) but ground contact time remains high — strides improve turnover mechanics and reduce braking forces, supporting the cadence gains you’re already achieving.

weekly_focus.description: Maintain high-volume Zone 1–2 running to solidify endurance gains while reintroducing brief, controlled neuromuscular stimuli to preserve pace responsiveness and running economy.
suggested_sessions: 3 × 3 min Z3 intervals w/ 90 sec recovery
